memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Say to them: 'For the generations to come, if any of your descendants
is ceremonially unclean and yet comes near the sacred offerings that
the Israelites consecrate to the LORD, that person must be cut off
from my presence. I am the LORD'" - Lev 22:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a solemn warning. A priest who knowingly came to the sacred
offerings while ceremonially unclean was to be cut off. The issue was
not that he had become unclean - that happened to everyone and was
normally easy to remedy. The issue was coming near anyway, as though
it did not matter.

That is presumption. It is knowing what God has said and deciding it
does not apply to you.

Dear reader, God has never asked us to be perfect before we come to
Him. But He does ask us to come honestly. There is a great difference
between the person who says, "Lord, I am unclean, wash me," and the
person who walks in pretending everything is fine while quietly
holding on to sin.

David wrote that if he had cherished sin in his heart, the Lord would
not have listened (Ps 66:18). Not because God is unwilling, but because
we are unwilling to be dealt with.

The wonderful news is that cleansing is always available. If we confess
our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us and purify us
from all unrighteousness (1 John 1:9). The door is open. We simply must
come through it, not around it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I holding on to something while pretending before God that I am
   not?
2. What would honest confession look like for me today?
3. Do I believe God's cleansing is truly available to me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I do not want to come to You pretending. Search me, show me what
I am hiding, and wash me clean through Jesus. Amen.
